title: Machine Learning
subtitle: From linear models to transformers and reinforcement learning, at the depth of Stanford CS229 and Berkeley CS189.
preface: This book covers the core of a graduate-level introduction to machine learning: supervised learning, kernel methods and trees, neural networks, unsupervised and generative models, probabilistic modeling, learning theory and reinforcement learning. The coverage follows the topics of Stanford CS229 and Berkeley CS189/289A, with the deep learning material of CS230 and CS182 and the reinforcement learning basics of CS234 added at the end.

Every method is derived, not just stated. Each chapter starts from a problem, builds a model, defines a loss, and then solves it, so you can see where each formula comes from and which assumptions it carries.

Machine learning rests on three subjects, and each has its own book in this library. Mathematics supplies linear algebra, calculus, probability and optimization. Computer Science supplies programming, algorithms, numerical computing and automatic differentiation. Data Science supplies data handling, statistical inference and experimental design. A term that is explained in any of these books is linked where it appears, so you can follow it back to its source and return with the Back button.
A reading order that works: read Linear Algebra and Probability in the Mathematics book first, then Parts I and II here, then Optimization, then the rest.
